defaults.permitted_development: Across Hampshire, change of use turns on the lawful existing use, the proposed use class and whether any specific permitted development route applies. In practice, frontage works, servicing, hours, noise and activity levels usually matter as much as the class label itself.

rules.height_rules: There is no automatic height allowance for change of use. Any new storey, plant, flue, lift overrun or rooftop equipment is separate operational development and needs its own assessment.
rules.depth_rules: There is no fixed depth allowance. Rear additions, yards, seating areas, storage compounds or service bays are separate planning questions from the use change itself.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Hampshire, the harder boundary issues are usually noise, servicing, odour, parking, deliveries, waste storage and the intensity of comings and goings near neighbouring occupiers.
rules.roof_rules: A use change does not automatically carry roof plant, vents, extraction kit or terraces with it. Those elements are assessed in their own right and can be the deciding issue for neighbours and design.
rules.materials_rules: Any external alterations such as shutters, signage, cladding, vents or changed openings should be judged as part of the wider street scene rather than as a minor afterthought to the use change.

rules.permitted_development: Change of use is not governed by a broad householder-style right. rules.height_rules: There is no automatic height envelope for change of use. New plant, flues, roof equipment or added storeys are assessed separately. In Basingstoke and Deane, any new plant or roof bulk is usually judged against nearby housing rather than against the use-change principle itself.
rules.depth_rules: There is no fixed depth allowance. Rear extensions, outdoor seating, storage yards, service bays or enlarged floorspace are separate planning issues from the use change itself.
rules.boundary_rules: For boundaries, the practical test is usually operational rather than dimensional: who arrives, when, where things are stored and what neighbours experience at the edge of the site. In Basingstoke and Deane, the harder boundary issues are usually parking, comings and goings, noise and overlooking from the changed use.
rules.roof_rules: New extract systems, vents, condensers, plant screens or roof terraces are not covered just because the use changes. They need their own planning assessment and can be decisive for neighbours.
rules.materials_rules: External alterations such as shopfront changes, shutters, signage, cladding or new openings are assessed separately and should fit the host building and the wider street scene. In visitor-heavy coastal areas, parking pressure, seasonal use and disturbance to nearby homes often attract closer scrutiny.

restrictions.conservation_area: Within a conservation area, frontage changes, plant, servicing and activity levels are often assessed just as closely as the use-class question itself.
